Metamodel Studio

Generate a PlantUML class diagram from text, an image, or both.

PNG, JPG, WEBP, or GIF; maximum 8 MB. Images are sent to the configured AI model. Do not upload confidential material without authorization.

Ready.

PlantUML source

Preview explicitly sends the PlantUML source to kroki.io. You can edit the source before previewing or saving it.

Validate structural constraints

Write requirements in natural language. An LLM translates them into a restricted rule format; a deterministic JavaScript engine checks the PlantUML source. No LLM decides whether a rule passes.

No validation run.

Supported checks: class existence, attribute existence/type, association, inheritance, and exact association-end multiplicity. Instance-level constraints are supported in the separate instance validation panel below. Unsupported constraints are reported as NOT EVALUATED, never silently passed.

Instance model editor

Create a JSON object model conforming to the current PlantUML metamodel. Objects have unique IDs, class types and attributes; links reference existing object IDs. The validator reads the current edited PlantUML source on every run.

Ready to generate instance models from the current metamodel.

The LLM proposes objects and links from your text using the current PlantUML metamodel. The server then runs deterministic conformance checks; it does not automatically repair invalid instances or claim they are valid.

Format: {"objects":[{"id":"...","type":"ClassName","attributes":{"field":value}}],"links":[{"source":"objectId","target":"objectId"}]}. Associations are checked against the PlantUML metamodel. Unspecified attributes are permitted; declared attributes are type-checked when present.

Instance constraints (OCL-inspired subset)

Write one requirement per line, or provide a structured rules JSON array to bypass the LLM. The LLM only maps natural language to the supported rule language. Every PASS/FAIL is computed by JavaScript, without LLM evaluation.

No instance validation run.

Deterministic checks include object types, attribute types, reference integrity, associations, declared multiplicities, uniqueness and supported attribute/link-count constraints. This is a restricted OCL-inspired rule language, not a full OCL interpreter. Unsupported expressions are NOT_EVALUATED.
